q: Not previously mentioned is the svarabhaktic glide which in a few instances was present between r and another consonant.

[Informant] also repeated ják̄iʃ. This ja is very uncertain − probably she said svarabhaktic e
1921, María de los Angeles Colós, José Guzman, and John Peabody Harrington, Chochenyo Field Notes:

e: From Swedish Svanberg + -ite, named after Swedish chemist Lars Fredrik Svanberg (1805–1878).
Borrowed from Sanskrit स्वरभक्ति (svára-bhakti, “vowel separation”), a compound of स्वर (svára, “vowel”) + भक्ति (bhaktí, “separation”).
